description: Digital-only, no-fee credit card for Brazil, founded by David Vélez to attack incumbents that charged among the world's highest banking fees. At seed, a Colombian outsider with Sequoia capital and zero product in a market of five oligopolistic banks.
current_status: NYSE:NU market cap ~$71B (April 2026). 123M customers across Brazil, Mexico, Colombia. Profitable since 2023, trailing-12-month revenue $10.6B, EPS compounding ~45%/yr. The highest-return early-stage bet in Latin American venture history.

founder.name: David Vélez
founder.background: Colombian, Stanford MBA, ex-Sequoia partner running LATAM investments — saw financial exclusion first-hand growing up, then saw it again on every deal flow spreadsheet.
founder.problem_fit: HIGH on vision — from the VC seat he had mapped the Brazilian banking oligopoly better than any incumbent insider. MEDIUM on operations — had never run a bank or underwritten credit.
founder.execution_evidence: Recruited Cristina Junqueira (ex-Itaú credit operations) as co-founder to close the banking-ops gap. Built from zero to 100M+ customers, IPO at $41B.
founder.red_flags: At founding: no banking-license experience, no card-issuing ops history.

stage_context.vs_base: Nubank outperforms pre-seed base rate in thriving (+9pp) and breakout (+6pp) driven by founder quality (ex-Sequoia VC), category-defining TAM (Brazilian banking oligopoly at extortionate spreads), and product simplicity. But at pre-seed, gravity still places most-likely tier at surviving (22pp) — no product yet, no regulatory moat, incumbent retaliation unmodeled.

verdict: Nubank survives IF (a) the founder team can hire bank-grade ops without adopting bank culture, (b) Bradesco/Itaú do not retaliate via regulation before product/market fit, (c) BCB allows a non-bank to issue cards at scale. At pre-seed most fragile: (b) — no evidence the incumbents will stay passive.
top_risk: Incumbent regulatory capture: five banks control 82% of deposits and have tight BCB relationships
top_opportunity: Brazilian consumers pay 200-450% APR on credit cards — a single-digit-APR insurgent captures massive share if allowed to operate
actual_outcome: The thesis held. Incumbents underestimated the threat; BCB stayed hands-off. By 2018 Nubank had 4M customers; by 2021 IPO at $41B; by 2026 one of the top-5 largest banks in Latin America by customer count. 1000x+ on Kaszek's seed position — the single bet that defined the franchise.
